headword: たこ{足|あし}{配線|はいせん}

definitions.gloss: octopus wiring; overloading a single electrical outlet
definitions.explanation: Running many appliances off one wall socket through stacked adapters and power strips, so the cords spread out like an octopus's legs. Treated in Japan as a well-known fire hazard.

examples.japanese: たこ{足|あし}{配線|はいせん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{危|あぶ}ない→危ない：00768_abunai⟧。
⟦{机|つくえ}→机：00762_tsukue⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{下|した}→下：00670_shita⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧たこ{足|あし}{配線|はいせん}になっている。
examples.english: Under the desk it's turned into a tangle of octopus wiring.

examples.japanese: ⟦{火事|かじ}→火事：01283_kaji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{原因|げんいん}→原因：01400_genin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧たこ{足|あし}{配線|はいせん}だった⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{消防署|しょうぼうしょ}→消防署：06454_shoubousho⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発表|はっぴょう}した→発表する：25231_happyousuru⟧。
examples.english: The fire department announced that the cause of the fire was octopus wiring.

notes:
From たこ (octopus) plus ⟦{配線|はいせん}→配線：07862_haisen⟧ (wiring): one socket with cords radiating from it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- たこ{足|あし}{配線|はいせん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to end up as octopus wiring
- たこ{足|あし}{配線|はいせん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{避|さ}ける→避ける：02109_sakeru⟧: to avoid overloading an outlet
- たこ{足|あし}{配線|はいせん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧: octopus wiring is hazardous

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase appears constantly in fire-prevention posters and household safety advice, so most Japanese speakers meet it as a warning rather than a technical term. It is also used figuratively for any overloaded single point, such as one worker handling too many jobs.
